question: subtilis LOD 与 4096-item 容量对 4.2M 三角形 / 2909 绘制对象 Bistro 场景的实际渲染增益

config.render: deferred lit path, shadow/taa/fxaa/bloom/ssao off, 1280x720, 130-frame offscreen captures
config.validation: off for the 2x2 wall/CPU matrix, on for the 3x3 GPU cross-check matrix
config.temporary_builder_probe: DEREN_BISTRO_BUILD builds the subtilis hierarchies at import; applied identically to OFF and ON, reverted after the runs (patch archived here)

capacity_unlock_vs_old_1024_build.note: the same scene on the previous build (1024-item admission) fell back to the legacy whole-frame geometry path; those numbers are the prior review logs (16-frame captures, gbuffer_debug=on, far camera)

method.cluster_dump: temporary engine probe DEREN_CLUSTER_PROBE_DUMP: camera view/proj, extent, and every visible item's world matrix + its meshlets' object-space bounding spheres/triangle counts, dumped on the first recorded frame (2-frame OFF capture, i.e. the full dispatch candidate set)
method.depth_dump: existing engine path DEREN_DEPTH_PROBE_CAPTURE: raw D32 depth of the screenshot frame
method.offline_analysis: scripts/measure/cluster_occlusion_probe.py - frustum test matching the mesh stage (conservative sphere), max-depth pyramid HZB occlusion test biased CONSERVATIVE (lower bound), projected cluster diameter bins
method.validation: projected sphere centres land on rendered geometry 99.74% (far) / 99.35% (near); depth foreground cover 17.36% (far) / 93.34% (near) matches the screenshots; the y convention is verified, and for the near camera both conventions agree within 0.35 pp

reading.frustum: the visibility lane already culls only 0-2% at the meshlet level: a compute pass that culled BEFORE the dispatch has no frustum-only win worth building
reading.occlusion: occlusion is the real headroom, and it is camera-dependent: far 0.4% of visible triangles vs near 32.5% (conservative lower bound) - an HZB two-pass target for interior/street views, near-useless for the distant overview
reading.subpixel: subpixel clusters are the opposite: far 22% of clusters (21% of triangles) below 1 px vs near 3% - the software-raster (Nanite-style) criterion is met at distance, not up close

cpu_selection_parallelization.change: record_visibility_items split into: serial candidate scan -> parallel per-item planning (process-wide 2-8 thread pool, per-worker scratch, disjoint writes into the host-culled lane) -> item-ordered publication rule resolved with an ordered interval table (overlapping items re-planned in order) -> serial recording; the old per-item O(n^2) published scan is gone

correctness.overlap_semantics: test_subtilis_frame alias case (two items sharing meshlet_base) still falls back the later item to the shared run - covered by the full CTest

gpu_frame.note: the GPU delta this session is smaller than the first matrix (-1.06/-1.31 ms against -2.2 ms); the absolute GPU times also drifted ~2-4 ms across sessions on this laptop, so the relative gain stays in the measured 4-9% range. The parallelization itself does not change GPU work.

runtime_screen_error_budget.hook: temporary DEREN_SUBTILIS_ERROR_PX override on view_parameters.target_error_px (default 1 px); removed again
runtime_screen_error_budget.result: 1 -> 4 px changes the selected record count by only ~1% and the GPU time not at all (inside the session noise): the cut is NOT limited by its error budget, so a runtime quality/perf knob here is not worth wiring.

builder_options.hook: temporary DEREN_BISTRO_OPTIONS "target_ratio,max_error" on build_options (defaults target_ratio .5, max_error .01); removed again
builder_options.result: target_ratio .35 / max_error .03 (alone or together) move the selected record count by <= 1% and the GPU time not at all: the hierarchy parameters are not leaving measurable savings on the table either.

tuning_experiments_2026_10_20.conclusion: Both cheap tuning levers are exhausted. The measured remaining headroom is structural: near-view occlusion (33% of visible triangles, conservative lower bound -> HZB two-pass) and far-view subpixel clusters (22% below 1 px -> software raster). Those are the next implementation steps; neither is reachable by parameter tuning.

m3_host_occlusion_prototype_2026_10_20.what_was_tried: a host-side two-phase prototype (reverted afterwards, patch archived here): every frame copies the G-buffer depth into a per-frame-slot host-readable buffer; the next use of that slot builds a max-depth Hi-Z pyramid on the CPU and the parallel planning phase filters the cut-selected meshlets whose bounding sphere is fully behind it, re-publishing the survivors and shrinking each item's dispatch. Static-camera only (a matrix comparison disables it in motion); off unless DEREN_OCCLUSION_CULL is set.

reading.gpu_saving_is_real: near view: 35% of the selected records culled -> GPU visibility raster 20.79 -> 14.16 ms (-31.9%) and GPU total 21.77 -> 15.61 ms (-28.3%). far view: 0 records culled, GPU unchanged (matches the probe: far occlusion is negligible).
reading.host_cost_kills_most_of_it: the prototype costs +11.2 ms of CPU per frame (CPU post phase 6.70 -> 17.88 ms): the pyramid build plus 46k sphere tests. The near frame becomes CPU-bound (CPU active 18.95 ms against a 15.61 ms GPU frame), so the end-to-end gain is only 20.61 -> 18.70 ms (-9.3%) instead of the -28% the GPU alone offers.
reading.not_pixel_exact: near view changed 0.314% of pixels (mean channel-max diff 0.003/255, max 10): the near-depth approximation is not perfectly conservative, so the host test is not shippable as-is. far view was pixel-identical.
reading.conclusion: the occlusion headroom translates into GPU time and is worth building properly, but NOT on the host: move the HZB build and the conservative sphere test into a GPU pass (M2/M3: build the pyramid from the frame depth, cull before the dispatch, use the stencil/two-pass recovery) so the near-view GPU saving stays and the CPU cost disappears. Expected near-view gain for that design: on the order of the measured -28% GPU frame time.
